scope: Batch 7 — corporate accountability: the Lafarge cassation cluster, the US corporate ATS canon (Unocal, Talisman, Nestlé, Chiquita), and the BHRRC Corporate Legal Accountability portal as a cross-reference source. Confirmed items folded into the dataset in the same commit.

cross_reference_source.name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre — Corporate Legal Accountability
cross_reference_source.note: 300+ lawsuit profiles; the natural corporate counterpart to TRIAL/UJAR/CFJ/Amnesty cross-references. The site blocks automated fetching (403), so profiles must be linked manually per case.

decisions_for_existing_cases.note: The corporate-complicity landmark: knowingly paying several million dollars to an organisation whose object is exclusively criminal suffices to characterise complicity in crimes against humanity, regardless of pursuing a commercial activity. Partial cassation reinstating the CAH complicity mise en examen track. Sibling arrêts of the same day: 19-87.031 (JURITEXT000044105519), 19-87.036 (JURITEXT000044105520, endangerment of employees), 19-87.040.
Procedural step in the Lafarge saga (chambre criminelle referring a question to another chamber) — verify posture before ingestion.

new_case_candidates_folded: us-doe-unocal — Doe v. Unocal (9th Cir. 2002 + C.D. Cal. 2000; settled 2005) — first corporate ATS case to survive toward trial; forced labour on the Yadana pipeline
us-talisman-sudan — Presbyterian Church of Sudan v. Talisman Energy (S.D.N.Y. 2003/2006; 2d Cir. 582 F.3d 244 (2009) purpose standard; cert denied 2010)

us-nestle-doe — Doe v. Nestlé/Cargill (9th Cir. 2014/2018/2019; SCOTUS Nestlé USA v. Doe, 17 June 2021 — general corporate activity in the US insufficient post-Kiobel; incorporates Jesner's bar on foreign-corporation ATS liability)

us-chiquita-mdl — In re Chiquita Brands (S.D. Fla. MDL 08-md-01916: 2011/2016/2018 opinions; June 2024 — first US jury verdict holding a corporation liable for financing paramilitary abuses, $38.3M; preceded by the 2007 DOJ guilty plea, $25M fine)
coverage_notes: FRENCH LOWER COURTS: LDH's French case-law sources are the Cour de cassation (three feeds), Conseil d'État, Conseil constitutionnel, CNDA and regulators — NO cours d'appel, tribunaux correctionnels/judiciaires or cours d'assises. French trial-level judgments in the corpus's cases (assises verdicts, the coming Lafarge trial, Amesys/Nexa chambre de l'instruction arrêts) are not systematically published anywhere official; sources remain FIDH/ECCHR/TRIAL dossiers and registry copies. The CNDA source (423 docs) is a promising vein for art. 1F exclusion decisions — connection dropped mid-probe; retry in a follow-up pass.
JESNER v. ARAB BANK, 584 U.S. 241 (2018) — the foreign-corporation ATS bar; not pinned to an LDH URL this pass (retrievable on CourtListener); referenced in the Nestlé fold summary.

SWEDEN/LUNDIN: the Stockholm District Court's Lundin trial (ongoing since Sept 2023; corpus case sweden-lundin-sudan) and the HD's 2021 jurisdiction ruling are not in LDH's Swedish digest sources — keep official domstol.se releases.
